page: Vultr voc-m-16c-128gb-1600s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server instance featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 8 physical AMD EPYC cores with 2 threads per core. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. It is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. Local storage is bundled with 1600 GB of NVMe SSD capacity, and the instance includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results indicate a strong single-core performance profile. In stress-ng single-core CPU testing, the server achieves a top-tier rating, placing in the top 10% of tested instances. Multi-core CPU performance, measured by stress-ng and Geekbench, falls within the average range. Memory performance is robust, with Passmark memory scores ranking in the top 25%, while raw memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks remain in the average tier. For language model workloads, the instance demonstrates strong text generation speeds for small 135M models, though prompt processing and larger 7B model inference speeds are average.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the server delivers a high density of dedicated AMD EPYC resources and local NVMe storage without the premium of GPU-accelerated hardware. The combination of 128.0 GB of RAM and 1600 GB of fast NVMe storage makes this instance suitable for memory-intensive and database workloads. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems, software compilation, and moderate-scale web serving.
